chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas, the freedman of Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who veils a good deed equals seventy good deeds, and the one who broadcasts an evil deed is forsaken, and the one who veils an evil deed is forgiven.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of hiding good deeds versus showing off bad deeds in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi distinguishes between 'istitrar' (concealment) and 'khumul' (hiding), emphasizing that modesty in good deeds multiplies their reward, while publicizing sins invites divine abandonment. The Imam’s statement reflects the principle that Allah prefers to forgive those who cover their faults, contrasting the spiritual elevation of hidden virtue with the exposure of vice. This concept underscores the importance of sincerity (ikhlas) and humility in personal piety.
